title: Australia's Services Sector Slips Back Into Contraction as S&P Global PMI Falls Below 50
body: Australia's services sector moved back into contraction territory in October, as the S&P Global Services PMI fell to 47.8, down sharply from 51.9 in September 2026. The October 2026 reading, updated on 22 October 2026, marks a notable reversal from the previous month, when the index had remained in expansionary territory above the 50 threshold. The drop below 50 signals a broad weakening in business activity across Australia's services industry, suggesting softer demand and potentially rising headwinds for the broader economy. With services making up a substantial share of Australia's economic output, the latest PMI data will likely heighten concerns about the momentum of growth heading into the final quarter of 2026, and may influence expectations around policy responses and corporate outlooks in the coming months. title: Australia's Manufacturing Slump Eases Slightly as S&P Global PMI Edges Up to 49.7 in October
body: Australia's factory sector showed a marginal improvement in October, with the S&P Global Manufacturing Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) ticking up to 49.7 from 49.6 in September 2026, according to data updated on 22 October 2026. Despite the uptick, the indicator remains below the 50.0 threshold that separates expansion from contraction, signaling that Australian manufacturing is still in a mild downturn. The 0.1-point increase suggests that while conditions remain under pressure, the pace of contraction has eased slightly compared with September. Investors and policymakers are likely to view the latest reading as a sign of tentative stabilization rather than a turnaround, with markets waiting to see whether subsequent months can push the index sustainably back into expansionary territory. title: Australia's Private Sector Slips Back Into Contraction as S&P Global PMI Falls Below 50 in October
body: Australia's combined S&P Global Manufacturing & Services PMI slid into contraction territory in October 2026, signaling a renewed soft patch for private sector activity. The index dropped to 47.70 in October from 51.30 in September, on a month‑over‑month basis, according to data updated on 22 October 2026. The September reading of 51.30 had indicated modest expansion in business activity across manufacturing and services, but the fall below the 50.0 threshold in October points to a reversal of momentum. On a comparative basis, the "Actual" October figure reflects a weaker performance versus the previous month, whereas the "Previous" figure captures September's improvement over August. The shift from expansion to contraction suggests that business conditions deteriorated over the latest month, with the headline PMI highlighting a broad-based cooling across Australia's private sector at the start of the final quarter of 2026. title: Ibovespa Drops as Investors Eye Presidential Runoff
body: The Ibovespa fell 1.1% on Thursday, closing at 204,120 points, pressured by uncertainty over the presidential race and corporate earnings. On Wednesday, a Quaest poll showed Flávio Bolsonaro's advantage over Lula shrinking to just one percentage point, leaving the two candidates statistically tied only four days before Sunday's presidential runoff. Many market participants see a Flávio Bolsonaro administration as more inclined to curb public spending, although neither the candidate nor his economic team has presented detailed fiscal adjustment plans. A new presidential voting-intention survey by Datafolha is scheduled for release after Thursday's market close. Financial stocks retreated, with Itaú down 1.8%, Itaúsa off 2.6%, and Bradesco losing 2.1% ahead of its earnings report later in the day. Vale dropped 4% amid lower iron ore prices, with the company due to publish quarterly results next week. WEG slipped 2.7%, extending Wednesday's 7% plunge following weaker-than-expected earnings. title: Fed Reserve Balances Slip Below $3 Trillion, Signaling Ongoing Liquidity Drain
body: Reserve balances with Federal Reserve Banks in the United States have declined, slipping back below the $3 trillion mark. The latest reading shows balances at $2.969 trillion, down from the previous level of $3.030 trillion, according to data updated on 22 October 2026. The move underscores a continuing reduction in liquidity parked at the Federal Reserve, a trend often associated with balance sheet runoff or shifts in banks' demand for reserves. While the data alone does not reveal the underlying drivers, the drop in reserve balances may influence short-term funding conditions and is likely to be closely watched by market participants tracking the stance and transmission of U.S. monetary policy. Investors and analysts will be monitoring subsequent releases to see whether this decline marks the start of a more pronounced downtrend or a temporary adjustment around the closely watched $3 trillion threshold in the banking system's reserve holdings. title: Fed's Balance Sheet Edges Lower to $6.754 Trillion, Signalling Ongoing Quantitative Tightening
body: The U.S. Federal Reserve's balance sheet slipped slightly to $6,754 billion, down from a previous level of $6,756 billion, according to the latest data updated on 22 October 2026. The marginal decline of $2 billion reflects the continuation of the Fed's cautious balance sheet reduction process. While the move is modest in size, it aligns with the central bank's broader effort to normalize monetary policy after years of aggressive asset purchases. The ongoing trimming of holdings is being closely watched by investors, as changes in the Fed's balance sheet can influence liquidity conditions, longer-term interest rates, and overall financial market sentiment. Market participants are likely to interpret the small week-on-week shift as a sign that the Fed is maintaining its gradualist approach, seeking to reduce support without disrupting funding markets or broader economic stability. With the balance sheet still elevated at $6.754 trillion, any future adjustments will remain a key focus for bond traders and analysts tracking the trajectory of U.S. monetary policy. title: TSX Drops on Oil Rally and BoC Hike Bets
body: The S&P/TSX Composite Index fell 1% to close at 35,973 on Thursday, as rising oil prices stoked inflation worries and strengthened expectations that interest rates will remain higher for longer. Crude prices advanced amid escalating tensions in the Middle East. Markets are now pricing in additional rate hikes from both the Bank of Canada and the US Federal Reserve this year, pressuring credit-sensitive sectors as investors weigh the impact of energy-driven inflation and higher borrowing costs. Financials were weaker, with major banks declining; Scotiabank slipped 0.9%. Miners also posted steep losses as gold prices retreated: Agnico Eagle fell 6.2%, Wheaton Precious Metals dropped 6.8%, Barrick lost 5.5%, and Franco-Nevada declined 5%. Technology stocks came under pressure after a lackluster earnings season from US megacaps rekindled concerns about the sustainability of AI-related spending. Celestica slumped 12% ahead of its results due Monday, while Shopify lost 3.5%. In contrast, Waste Connections jumped nearly 9.5% after reporting better-than-expected profit and revenue and raising its full-year outlook. title: Wall Street Falls as Tech Sell-Off Deepens
body: US equity markets finished lower on Thursday, weighed down by a broad sell-off in technology shares. The S&P 500 declined 1.2%, the Nasdaq slid 2.9%, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average ended little changed. Tech stocks came under pressure as recent earnings reports underwhelmed, reigniting doubts about the durability of the AI-driven rally and extending the ongoing rotation out of semiconductor names. Meta dropped 7% despite posting higher earnings and revenue, as its credit risk rose to a record high. The company's plans to significantly increase capital expenditures revived concerns that large tech firms will take on additional debt to fund AI-related infrastructure. Other major cloud and AI players also retreated ahead of their results next week, with Alphabet down 3.2%, Microsoft off 2.2%, and Amazon falling 4.6%. Tesla slid 3.1% after paring back its spending plans, with last quarter's capital expenditures coming in below market expectations. Lam Research sank 11.8% following a weaker-than-expected outlook. Among semiconductor stocks, Nvidia fell 4.4%, Micron declined 6.3%, AMD plunged 8.1%, and Intel lost 8%. The material has been provided by InstaForex Company - www.instaforex.com

title: Oil Tops $99 as Middle East Tensions Escalate
body: Crude oil climbed above $99 a barrel on Thursday, its highest level in more than a month, as escalating tensions in the Middle East and reports of planned US strikes on Iran rattled markets. According to reports, US and Israeli military officials have drawn up plans for renewed attacks after next month's midterm elections, with Iran's energy infrastructure expected to be a primary target. The US has also ordered non-emergency government personnel and their families to leave Saudi Arabia, following an uptick in attacks by Iran-aligned Houthi forces. The directive was issued after an attack on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam, on Saudi Arabia's east coast, on Wednesday. In a further sign of heightened security concerns, Saudi Aramco has reportedly told employees to evacuate its headquarters in Dhahran and work remotely. Aramco facilities have been repeatedly targeted by Houthi attacks in recent years. Together, these developments have intensified fears of prolonged disruptions to oil supplies from the region. title: Argentina's Retail Sales Surge in August
body: Argentina's retail sales rose 24.3% year-on-year to ARS 698.56 billion in August 2026, accelerating from a 23% increase in July. Among the main categories, entertainment and leisure posted the strongest expansion, up 62.8%, followed by furniture, home décor and textiles (41.6%), sporting goods and accessories (36.4%), and perfumery and pharmacy (33%). Sales at food courts, food outlets and kiosks advanced 28.1%, while bookstore and stationery sales and other categories each grew 26.1%. Clothing, footwear and leather goods increased 17%, and toy sales were up 13.5%. Electronics, household appliances and computing was the only segment to contract, slipping 4%. Regionally, retail sales climbed 31.6% in the Autonomous City of Buenos Aires and 20.4% across the 24 districts of Greater Buenos Aires. In the rest of the country, sales rose 20.1% in the Pampas region and 23.9% in Cuyo, while the Northern and Patagonia regions recorded increases of 21.9% and 32.2%, respectively.
